idiom_name: structural interface view contract + typed presenter class (object-literal doubles)
implementation_notes: TypeScript interfaces are erased at runtime and checked structurally, so the view contract is a compile-time type the presenter is written against; neither the concrete view nor a test double needs to declare `implements` - an object literal with the right members satisfies the interface, which removes the classic structure's inheritance ceremony. Keep DOM access, framework imports and event registration inside the view module, type the presenter against the interface, and inject a fake in tests. Keep an abstract class instead only when the view needs shared implementation; use the interface when the contract is the only thing that must be enforced.
pitfalls: Structural typing accepts a double that satisfies the type by accident (wrong units, extra members); assert the calls the presenter makes, not only the shape of the fake.
Interfaces vanish at runtime, so wiring done by string or framework convention is unchecked; keep the event registration in the concrete view and compile-check it against the interface.
Component frameworks (React, Angular, Vue) provide their own state separation; running an MVP presenter alongside component state creates two sources of truth.
